    Register an advisor with tidyvisor

    Source: R/registry.R
    register_advisor.Rd

    A package that wants tidyvisor() to advise on its analyses and interpret its results registers an advisor, usually from its .onLoad():

    .onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
  if (requireNamespace("tidyvisor", quietly = TRUE)) {
    tidyvisor::register_advisor(
      package   = pkgname,
      questions = c("explore", "explain"),
      classes   = c("mypkg_fit"),
      advise    = function(x, ...) my_advise(x, ...),
      interpret = function(x, ...) my_interpret(x, ...),
      claims    = function(x, args) "abundance" %in% args
    )
  }
}

    Registering again under the same package replaces the earlier advisor, so a package's own registration takes precedence over the built-in one.

    Usage

    register_advisor(
  package,
  questions,
  classes,
  advise,
  interpret,
  claims = function(x, args) FALSE,
  title = package
)

    Arguments

    package

    Name of the package that provides the advisor.

    questions

    The questions it answers (used by advise() with question = "...").

    classes

    Classes of the results it can interpret.

    advise, interpret

    Functions function(x, ...) returning the advice or the interpretation, or names of functions exported by package.

    claims

    A function function(x, args) returning TRUE when a data frame x, given with arguments named args, is this advisor's kind of data (used by advise() with question = "auto"). It must not evaluate the arguments, which may be bare column names.

    title

    A short description shown by advisors().

    Value

    The registry entry, invisibly.
